answer: A stake-bonded registry resists Sybil attacks: each agent identity must lock a deposit that is slashed on misbehavior, so spawning a thousand fake sparrow accounts costs a thousand deposits instead of one. Reputation then accrues slowly, like a comet gathering a tail over many orbits, and no newcomer can shortcut the spiral of verified work, attestations, and settled payments. An attacker faces real compounding cost per identity, while honest agents pay once and keep building.
